findings.title: Unbounded `limit` on public members endpoint
findings.body: `limit` comes straight from `params[:limit]` with no upper bound. The previous code capped results at 200 (and only for automatic groups). Any client can now pass a huge limit and force a very large query and serialization. Negative values are also not guarded: a negative offset or limit would raise a database error or be passed through to SQL. Clamp both values.

findings.title: remove_member deletes via `users.delete(user_id)` on a possibly non-member
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an integer to a has_many :through association. That depends on Rails accepting ids there, and it does not use the `group.remove` API that the old code used. The old API probably kept `group_users` and the denormalized user counts consistent. A non-member id is silently ignored, so the endpoint reports success regardless. Use `group.remove(User.find(...))` instead.

findings.title: totalPages off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and a limit of 50 it shows 2 pages, and `next` then goes to an empty page. It should use `Math.ceil`.

findings.title: addMembers does not clear the input and the group-members UI isn't reset on failure
findings.body: After `addMembers` the `usernames` field is left populated, as the TODO admits. Clicking Add twice re-sends the same usernames. The call also has no error handler, so server errors such as the 422 for automatic groups are swallowed with no feedback.

findings.title: Members route no longer waits for data
findings.body: `findMembers()` is now called in `setupController` without being returned or awaited. The template renders an empty or stale `members` list first, and `{{#if model}}` is always true, so the table header shows with no rows during loading. Errors from the call are also unhandled.
